item.title: A Sense of Ease
item.description:
A prepared speech for Toastmasters, and the first episode of Spontaneous Prose. The club topic was “a sense of ease.” Joyce reads what kept her up at night: urgent work versus what actually feels important, and why being present is so hard when the list never ends.

Takeaway: she does not have a solution. When the question gets too loud, she gets out of bed, turns on the light, and speaks it into a microphone.

Opening music: Andrii H, background (Pixabay).

Chapters

TimeTopic
0:00Opening music.
0:07Welcome to Spontaneous Prose; tonight’s topic is a sense of ease.
0:49Ease as another word for being present, and the years that stopped feeling that way.
2:32Urgent versus important: the two-by-two matrix that will not line up.
5:07The list keeps growing, and Toastmasters still gets missed.
5:31Why some people seem to have a career, a body, and a family all at once.
6:14No solution — spit it out at two in the morning, then the light goes off.
